newsitem.title: INDIA: India to set up panel for domestic coffee futures.
newsitem.headline: India to set up panel for domestic coffee futures.

text.p: Indian state-run Coffee Board officials and private traders have agreed to form a committee to study the prospects of setting up a domestic coffee futures exchange, officials said on Wednesday.
They said the decision was taken after a one-day seminar on domestic coffee futures in the southern city of Bangalore.

"Exporters and Board officials have taken a decision to set up a core committee which would look into the areas of setting up of a domestic coffee futures exchange and how it would operate," a Coffee Board official told Reuters.
The committee would consist of government officials, private traders and exporters, he said.

The Economic Times newspaper said that the committee will have 16 members and will be chaired by Philipose Mathai, chairman of the Coffee Board. Shamik Bose of Adnani Exports will be the vice-chairman.
The daily said the committee would try to establish the exchange in Bangalore by December this year.
The newspaper quoted Mathai as saying that the proposed exchange would bring in more liquidity and funds to the industry.
"It is not our intention that all the over 100,000 growers will be accessing the proposed exchange," the daily quoted Mathai as saying.
"Hopefully, the small growers will be guided by associations and cooperatives who would be operating on the proposed exchange."
